records.title: Plague bacteriology and vaccination in Hong Kong/Bombay colonial public-health worlds
records.sourceNativeSummary: The 1894 Hong Kong plague epidemic produced competing bacteriological investigations by Yersin and Kitasato, followed by vaccine work such as Haffkine's Bombay program. Laboratory identification, field epidemiology, colonial authority and mass vaccination interacted under severe disease pressure.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Competing isolations and later rat/flea transmission knowledge show that identifying a bacterium did not immediately close the full transmission model. Colonial vaccination operated under asymmetric authority, making uptake and consequence inseparable from governance and local trust.

sources.supports: Haffkine Bombay plague vaccine production/trials and colonial context

records.title: Basic Bessemer correction and open-hearth competition in mass steelmaking
records.sourceNativeSummary: Thomas and Gilchrist's basic-lining process in the late 1870s attacked the phosphorus boundary left by acid Bessemer, while open-hearth steel continued as a slower route with different feedstock/control advantages. A major HD2 bottleneck therefore became a solvable chemistry/materials problem only after new process assumptions appeared.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The correction did not make one steel process universally optimal. Ore chemistry, scale, control and product requirements continued to select among Bessemer/basic/open-hearth routes; a once-material boundary can disappear without invalidating the earlier scoped diagnosis.

records.title: Wardenclyffe: global wireless/power vision without technical-financial closure
records.sourceNativeSummary: Tesla began Wardenclyffe in 1901 as a prototype for worldwide wireless communication and power. A 187-foot tower/lab was built, but the project exceeded financing and never became an operational global power system; work effectively ended by 1906.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Large vision, prior inventor reputation and some local electrical demonstrations did not establish long-range power-transfer viability. Financial failure and physical/scientific uncertainty are coupled but distinct; later wireless communication success should not retroactively validate wireless-power claims.

sources.supports: global wireless-power vision, financial failure and incomplete tower
non-operational tower, commercial skepticism and 1906 end

records.title: Ford pre-1903 failed automobile companies before later product/production fit
records.sourceNativeSummary: Ford's Detroit Automobile Company was a real manufacturing attempt that produced poor/marginal vehicles and closed in 1901; the Henry Ford Company also failed before the 1903 Ford Motor Company. Later success followed additional prototype/racing/product and organizational changes.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Later Model T/mass-production success does not show the earlier firms were secretly successful. Failure generated experience/reputation pressure and option value, but the declared business/product outcomes remained failures.

sources.supports: Detroit Automobile Company factory and product failure
two failed firms 1899–1902 and later third-attempt prototype

records.title: Koch tuberculin: true bacteriological authority followed by therapeutic overreach
records.sourceNativeSummary: After identifying the tuberculosis bacillus, Koch announced tuberculin in 1890 as a therapeutic/preventive remedy. It appeared promising in his laboratory/animal framework but failed spectacularly across human clinical practice; months later cure claims were disputed and discredited. Tuberculin later retained diagnostic value.
records.rivalOrBoundary: This is not evidence that Koch's tuberculosis-bacillus discovery was false. It is a direct boundary on authority transfer: validated causal expertise and local experimental response did not authorize a human-therapy claim under materially different disease conditions.

sources.supports: lab success versus clinical failure and disease-model mismatch
premature 1890 cure announcement and rapid debunking
therapy failure and later diagnostic reuse

records.antiCase: validated expertise/model in one claim does not transfer authority to adjacent therapy

records.title: Tesla–Ferraris independent rotating-field/polyphase induction-motor routes
records.sourceNativeSummary: Ferraris and Tesla independently developed rotating-magnetic-field/polyphase motor concepts during the 1880s; Tesla's 1888 motor/patents were commercialized by Westinghouse. The route linked AC generation/distribution to practical brushless motor loads.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Priority compression around Tesla alone hides independent Ferraris work and Westinghouse engineering. A motor principle required a compatible polyphase supply and manufacturable machine before it altered the power-system value proposition.

sources.supports: first commercial AC motor and polyphase field

records.title: Hall–Héroult independent aluminium electrolysis
records.sourceNativeSummary: In 1886 Hall in the United States and Héroult in France independently found molten-cryolite electrolysis routes that made commercial aluminium possible. Cheap electrical power and later alumina supply turned a rare precious metal into a mass material.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The near-simultaneous route demonstrates independent convergence, but electrolysis alone was not the whole industry: power cost, cryolite/alumina feed and capital-scale cells were necessary complements.

sources.supports: cryolite route, priority and capital/power context
